html:
Uncle Tom's Cabin is an anti-slavery novel by Harriet Beecher Stowe, published as a book in 1852. Written in Maine after the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850, it tells of the enslaved Tom, sold down the river, and Eliza, who escapes across the frozen Ohio River.

It sold 300,000 copies in its first year in the United States and over a million in Britain, the best selling novel of the century. Stage versions spread it further.

The book stirred anger at slavery in the North and fury in the South. A story says that Lincoln greeted Stowe as the little woman who made the great war, though it may not be true. Later readers criticised its racial stereotypes. It drew on the stories of escaped slaves such as Frederick Douglass and Josiah Henson, before the Civil War.
